defectsFound.summary: release:plan under-reports what release:build will re-run: it refreshes per-stage freshness but never applies the STAGE_DEPENDENCIES cascade fixpoint that build.ts applies, so stages that WILL be rebuilt are listed under 'READY (fresh)'.
defectsFound.where: src/release/plan.ts:39 (refreshStageStatuses, no propagation) vs src/release/build.ts:112-126 (the `while (propagated)` fixpoint); the misleading labels are src/release/plan.ts:103 ('READY (fresh)'), :107-112 ('STALE (will re-run on release:build)') and :86 ('(reruns: …)').
defectsFound.observed: After the content resolution, release:plan printed READY (fresh): reconstruction, template, theme, seo, assets, production / STALE: content / NEXT ACTION 12: 'pnpm release:build …   (reruns: content)'. release:build --dry-run on the very same state printed WOULD RUN: content, theme, seo, production. Same divergence in the theme scenario: plan said '(reruns: theme)' and listed production under READY, while the dry run said WOULD RUN theme, production — and the real build then re-ran both.
defectsFound.impact: An operator using the documented one-screen view (spec §14/§20) is told a rebuild is cheaper and narrower than it is, and is told production is fresh when it is about to be recompiled. The persisted stageStatus written by release:resolve has the same gap, so the state file is the origin of the wrong answer, not just the renderer.
defectsFound.notFixed: SUPERSEDED — see `fixed` below. (Original note: deliberately not fixed by this agent, which is validation, not construction; src/release/ was another agent's ownership. See changeRequests[0].)
defectsFound.fixedWhere: src/release/freshness.ts:367 `export function propagateStaleStages(stageStatus)` — the STAGE_DEPENDENCIES cascade fixpoint — is called from inside refreshStageStatuses at src/release/freshness.ts:343, and src/release/plan.ts:39 calls refreshStageStatuses. The cascade is therefore applied to the plan's own view, not only to build's. src/release/build.ts:113 records that its former local call site was folded into the shared refresh, and freshness.ts:340-342 states the intent: "The cascade is applied HERE, not at each call site: every consumer of a refresh (plan, build, resolve, prepare) must answer 'what will re-run?' identically, and the persisted stageStatus must carry that same answer." src/release/resolve.ts:160-163 persists that refreshed (cascaded) stageStatus, closing the "the state file is the origin of the wrong answer" half as well.
defectsFound.fixedVerifiedBy: Task 27 final-residuals agent, by reading the call chain at HEAD (baseline d33abb3 + the uncommitted Task 27 work). STATIC verification only: the plan-vs-dry-run divergence was NOT re-executed against data/linear.app/release-projects/flowpilot-wr27, so this is a code-path claim, not a fresh reproduction.

limitations: PREVIEW TARGET ONLY on the main project. The real build ran with target mode 'preview' and finished at PRODUCTION_INPUTS_REQUIRED — 88 release-blocking requirements (font licences, 84 replacement images, production domain, source brand SVG) remain genuinely unresolved for linear.app, exactly as Task 26 reported. An indexable-production build was therefore never executed end-to-end; the indexable path was exercised only as far as the BLOCKED BY gate on the throwaway project.

ONE SLOT, ONE TOKEN. The authoring surface was validated with a single cosmetic text slot and a single paint token. Bulk authoring (hundreds of slots), per-route slot values, url slots and asset/font resolutions were not exercised by this agent.

ASSETS STAGE NEVER RAN. assets depends only on template and the resolution carried no assets/fontDecisions, so applyAssetResolutions (src/release/resolve-assets.ts) is still unexercised on real data by this exercise.

The retry/resume proof used the runners injection seam. A genuine mid-build crash (process kill between stage saves) was not simulated, and no historical artifact was corrupted to force a natural failure — as instructed.
linear.app only. stripe.com lineage was deliberately not touched (scripts/smoke-release.ts reads it unguarded).

Sibling agents were writing to the same tree during the exercise (e.g. data/linear.app/page-regions/2026-08-26T16-14-07-901Z appeared from another agent). The typecheck and smoke:release results above describe the tree as it stood at 2026-08-26T19:20-19:30Z.
